failure_summary: The harness prompt suffix SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE (connect-four/server/scripts/compute.mjs:253-261) explicitly orders the model to "Refer to the two discs as verde ... and gris" and to copy cNrM cells verbatim inside `mechanism`, which directly contradicts A5a (no player colour names) and the grounded prompt line "Never write a raw square" — runs 1 and 2 duly say "al verde"/"del verde" (A5a fail 2/3) and run 0 duly wrote the raw "c4r3" as the inner text of [zone:future:c7r6], which guard P6 then stripped (guardDiagnostics.strippedSpecs=["future:c7r6"]), deleting the only reference to the fork pivot the requiredSet demands.
notes: 3 runs this run (not 5). A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-31T12-52-38Z_mechanical.json keys pin-L5-deep-fork|D|0..2 (all pass). Sub-sampled axes A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 = null (not scored, not a pass). | SPANISH-RUN LOCALE ARTIFACT (do not charge the model): run 0 servedExplanation reads "la pieza clave en column 4" — English inside Spanish prose. Reproduced computeServedExplanation(mechanism, render_decision, movestring, locale): the stored string is byte-identical to locale="en" output and differs from locale="es" output ("columna 4"). stripInternalTokens IS locale-aware (reasonRenderGuard.mjs:99-108) and production passes req.locale (index.js:1470), so a real es player would read "columna 4". This is an eval-harness artifact of computeServedExplanation being called without the locale (the --locale threading is uncommitted working-tree work, git diff compute.mjs:330/473), NOT an A5a failure. A5 for run 0 = pass on the locale-corrected served string. | A5 run 1 FAIL: "le dejás al verde la forma de cortar esa red" names a player by colour. A5 run 2 FAIL: "frenabas la jugada del verde" + "le dio al verde la forma de apagar esa idea" (colour x2) plus the untranslated English noun "fork" in "la casilla que creaba el fork". Both are directly instructed by SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE, so triage is render_bug, not model failure. | GUARD GAP (secondary, model-independent): checkP3 sub-check 2 (annotationGate.js:184) is /\b(Red|Yellow|Black)\b/gi. It does not catch "verde"/"gris" (or even English Green/Gray), and it FALSE-POSITIVES on the ordinary Spanish noun "red" (network) — that is the entire source of the P3:player_name diagnostic on runs 0 and 1 ("negar esa red" / "cortar esa red"), while run 2, which actually names a colour twice, reports failures:[]. The guard is exactly inverted on Spanish text. | A7 run 0 FAIL (A7b, A7c): served text says "la pieza clave en column 4" (unwrapped — its zone was stripped) and separately "[zone:future:c4r3]la casilla de la columna 4[/zone:future:c4r3]", so one column-4 phrase points at nothing and two phrases name the same object; and the requiredSet handle you-fork-pivot (spec future:c7r6, role "the square you play to CREATE the fork") is never named in the served string, so the pivot that creates the fork is unrecoverable. A7c is attributed, not excused: the pivot WAS offered (render_decision.zones.aliases you-fork-pivot) and is in requiredSet. | G7 run 0 FAIL (judgment half; G7a/G7b membership pass, annotationRepairs empty): [zone:future:c7r6] wraps the literal text "c4r3" — a different square from the handle spec, so the handle does not wrap a phrase whose meaning matches its role. | A4 run 1 FAIL: "Si jugás en la columna 1, creás la doble amenaza alrededor de la casilla que arma el quiebre" asserts a double threat is created NOW. visualize_board.sh 4222425320 (after-best) shows a single major threat, col2 row1 (O) — no fork. The fork lives 28 plies out (lostResource.pliesToEnd=28) on the projectedDeep board (visualize_board.sh 42224253201100134400101124465555566666: major threats col4 r3/r4/r5/r6). The prompt handle role says verbatim "not a threat right now" and instructs future/conditional language. Runs 0 ("mantenías viva") and 2 ("mas adelante, cuando esa secuencia forzada llegaba") do defer correctly, so this is run-1-only. | G2 runs 0-1 FAIL (guardrail half): link L5 guardrail is "You had a forced win; state its horizon honestly (may be deep)." Run 0 never states a forced win and closes by calling the better move "la defensa mas fuerte" (the strongest DEFENCE), which contradicts best_outcome=win; run 1 gives no horizon beyond "despues" and mis-states it as an immediate fork. Run 2 is the one that honours it ("mas adelante, cuando esa secuencia forzada llegaba") but G2 is null there by sub-sampling. No over-removal problem: every covers code the answers needed was present (D28). | A5b APPLIES BY ITS TRIGGER (player===2 AND boardState==="opening") but its clause "claiming to be building a win as the 2nd player also fails" is unsatisfiable here: fv.case is win_to_draw and the pre-computed A2 requires best_outcome="win". I did NOT fail A5b for reporting the win — charging it would contradict A2 and charge the model for ground truth. No run is defeatist, so A5b is otherwise satisfied. Flagging the rubric conflict rather than resolving it. | G4/G5 verified: every named cell (c4r3, c6r5, c7r6) lies on render_decision.finalMovestring 42224253201100134400101124465555566666 (plies 16/32/38 respectively); the rendered threat lists are board-true (afterBest: immediate at c2r1 you = col2 row1 (O) [GT]; projectedDeep: c4r3 you GT, c4r4 both, c4r5 you, c4r6 opp — all confirmed by visualize_board.sh). G3: afterPlayed is shown:false and no run needed it. G6: patternOnAfterBestBoard=null with route "sign" and link L5 for win_to_draw is the correct routing. | UNSCORED OBSERVATION (run 2, A4 is null by sub-sampling): "frenabas la jugada del verde" claims column 1 blocked the opponent. On the decision board (visualize_board.sh 422242532) column 1 carries only (o) minor threats and Green has nothing there — the claim is board-false and would fail A4 had run 2 been scored on it. | MODEL REGIME: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships — a production-fidelity run, not a floor test. Every attribution above is deliberately model-INDEPENDENT (a prompt suffix that orders the banned wording, a guard regex that is inverted on Spanish, a stripped span that removes a requiredSet referent); none rests on prompt_confusion.

counterexamples.evidence: Directive orders "Refer to the two discs as verde (first player) and gris (second player)"; runs 1 and 2 servedExplanation say "al verde"/"del verde", which A5a bans as naming a player by colour. The instruction and the rubric are in direct conflict.

/\b(Red|Yellow|Black)\b/gi fires on the Spanish noun "red" in "negar esa red" (run 0) and "cortar esa red" (run 1) while missing the actual colour naming in run 2, whose guardDiagnostics.failures is [].
